newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM PARTY'S LEAD WIDENS, HIS SUPPORT OFF - POLL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM PARTY'S LEAD WIDENS, HIS SUPPORT OFF - POLL.

text.p: The gap between Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) and the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) widened in March, though both parties' leaders fell further out of favour with voters.

A public opinion poll by the state research agency IVVM said showed that support for ODS edged up two percentage points from February to 26 percent, while the CSSD, falling to 19 percent from a previous 21 percent.

Ruling coalition partners the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) and the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) also lost support, falling to 12 percent and eight percent respectively. KDU was previously at 14 percent, ODA at 8.5 percent.
IVVM said, however, the number of undecided voters, rose to 22 percent from 16 percent in February, indicating possible shifts ahead in the electorate.

The far right Republican party (SPR-RSC) fell below the five percent minimum needed for parliamentary representation for the second time in three months, garnering only a three percent support rating.
The Communist party (KSCM), the only other party with parliamentary representation, eased to seven percent from eight percent.

The coalition lost its parliamentary majority in last June's elections, gaining 99 seats in the 200-seat chamber, but remained in power as the Social Democrats ruled out a grand coalition with the two extremist parties.
In a separate IVVM poll also released on Monday, 50 percent of voters surveyed said they distrust both Klaus and his avowed enemy, CSSD leader Milos Zeman.
President Vaclav Havel was also hard hit, though he remains the country's most-trusted politician, getting only a 68 percent trust rating, down some 14 percentage points from the last poll.
CSSD Vice-chairwoman Petra Buzkova was the only politician to post a significant gain in voter trust, rising 17 points to 57 percent.
Republican leader Miroslav Sladek entrenched his position as the most distrusted political figure in the Czech Republic, rising four points to 73 percent.
